ORIGINAL ARTWORK

Original painting

Make yourself comfortable

A few simple controls

Walk
WASD or arrow keys. Hold Shift to move faster. On a touch screen, use the left thumb control.
Look
Click Start walking for mouse look. You can also drag the view, or use J / L to turn and I / K to look up and down. On a touch screen, drag the right side.
Enter a painting
Walk through a large portal frame, or press E when its label appears. The smaller gallery paintings open their originals.
Find your way
Follow the paths and local map. Worlds takes you anywhere; Painting garden brings you home.
Take a tour
Guided walk takes you around the scene and returns to its entrance. Pause and resume whenever you like. Moving or dragging takes back control.
Release the mouse
Press Esc. Nothing is lost when you open a menu.

Painted scenery all around

The original brushwork is mapped onto the scene’s visible surfaces. Walk slowly to explore their depth, or turn to see the imagined surroundings. The view opens in the painting’s proportions; Expanded surroundings fills the screen with areas beyond the canvas.

Step through the canvas

Each entrance uses the artwork’s framing by default. The painting and scene keep the same scale when you compare them. Original painting opens the source canvas; click it again to return to where you were walking. Canvas viewpoint brings you back after exploring. Press C to compare or R to reset.

These are reconstructions with layered scenery and modeled objects. Short movements preserve more of the source composition. Larger walks reveal repaired textures and imagined sides; those areas cannot be verified from one painting. Original painting lets you compare the scene with its source.

Each of the nine environments is reconstructed from its own source painting. Unseen parts remain interpretations. All 61 source images are preserved in the garden and collection; not every painting has its own separate modeled world.

Scene names describe their subjects. “Lily Lake” follows the handwritten caption on its source painting.
